title: Evaluating Reading Comprehension Exercises Generated by LLMs: A Showcase of ChatGPT in Education Applications
venue: Proceedings of the 18th Workshop on Innovative Use of NLP for Building Educational Applications (BEA 2023)
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT can be used to generate high-quality, personalized English reading comprehension materials for school use, addressing a practical problem identified by middle school English teachers in China: students often reuse outdated reading passages and teachers face high workload when adapting texts and writing questions. The study asks whether a ChatGPT-based system can generate suitable reading passages and multiple-choice questions for middle school English learners, and whether such a system could be useful in real educational settings.

The authors build a reading exercise generation system with a graphical user interface that allows users to specify passage length, genre, difficulty level, and topic. ChatGPT is used in zero-shot and one-shot prompting modes to generate reading passages and comprehension questions, with an added toxicity check before materials are made available. The study also includes a GPT-2 + PPLM baseline for passage generation comparison. Evaluation combines automatic text metrics, structured human ratings of generated passages and questions, pairwise comparisons against human-written textbook materials, and qualitative feedback interviews from teachers who used the system.

The educational context is Chinese middle school English learning, especially Grades 7 to 9, with source materials and evaluation framed around reading comprehension exercises used in Beijing schools. Participants in the evaluations included Chinese college students with prior experience doing such exercises, native English speakers recruited online, and three experienced middle school teachers in Beijing who used the system for one week. The system is intended for teachers and students, but the direct first-hand implementation feedback comes primarily from teachers.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT-generated reading passages were rated as high quality and, in several human evaluations, even outperformed human-written textbook passages on dimensions such as readability, coherence, engagement, and overall quality. Generated questions were judged relevant to passages but weaker than human-written questions, especially because distractor options were often repetitive or low quality. Teachers reported that the system was useful, easy to use, and promising for providing diverse and personalized reading materials, though the authors note that broader deployment and more extensive user feedback are still needed.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical evaluation study with structured human assessment and limited teacher field feedback, but it does not measure K-12 student learning outcomes directly and lacks a causal design such as an RCT or strong quasi-experiment. Evidence is mainly based on content-quality ratings and qualitative implementation feedback.
impact_tier_rationale: Findings suggest promising but unclear educational impact: materials were judged high quality and teachers perceived workload benefits, yet no direct independent literacy gains or quantified effect sizes on student outcomes were reported.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-based system for generating personalized English reading comprehension passages and multiple-choice exercise questions for Chinese middle school learners, with editable outputs for teacher use and adaptation in school contexts.
Graphical reading-exercise generation system that delivers AI-generated reading practice materials through a teacher-facing interface for classroom or school-based English practice.

finding.finding_summary: The study found that ChatGPT-generated reading passages were rated as higher quality than both a fine-tuned GPT-2 baseline and, in several human evaluations, higher than human-written textbook passages for middle school English reading practice. In Human Evaluation 1, Chinese student raters scored ChatGPT passages higher than human-written passages on overall quality (4.46 vs. 4.18), readability (4.61 vs. 4.52), correctness (4.60 vs. 4.32), coherence (4.65 vs. 4.39), and engagement (4.37 vs. 4.07); however, no direct student learning gains were measured.
finding.measure: Human ratings of reading-passage quality, suitability, topic coherence, and comparison with textbook passages for English reading comprehension materials
finding.study_size: 30 human-written passages + 30 ChatGPT passages + 30 GPT-2 passages in Example Set 1; 10 human-written passages + 30 generated passages in Example Set 2; 9 Chinese college student evaluators and 36 native English speakers for passage evaluation

finding.finding_summary: Teachers reported that the system could substantially reduce the time and cost of creating diverse, personalized reading comprehension materials, and that output quality exceeded expectations despite weaknesses in distractor-option generation. This finding is based on one-week first-hand use and interview feedback from three experienced Beijing middle school teachers, without quantified time-savings or workload effect sizes.
finding.measure: Teacher interview feedback on usefulness, ease of use, and perceived reduction in workload/cost

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports that the system was utilized by middle school English teachers and was perceived as promising for school implementation, with teachers describing it as a personalized resource library that could support broader provision of diverse reading materials. However, this was based on limited pilot use and perception data rather than measured school-wide adoption or institutional outcomes.
finding.measure: Teacher perceptions of school applicability and implementation promise
